retail_intro: Retail heads into Presidents' Day holding stock bets it cannot trade until Tuesday, led by Trump's Truth Social launch: a classic buy-the-rumour setup, where the crowd prices a public date in advance and the event decides whether the first gap pays early holders or traps late ones.

retail.title: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — Truth Social launches on a closed market
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story the DWAC crowd tells itself fits on a bumper sticker: Trump's app goes live on Presidents' Day, and the ticker tied to his media company reprices the moment trading reopens. Digital World Acquisition, the SPAC for Trump Media & Technology Group, closed at 84.32 USD, up 15.32% from 73.12 USD on January 21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The pull is a lottery ticket with a cause attached: a wager that Trump can build the Twitter rival Forbes describes [[n1722]]. The holiday sharpens the itch: the catalyst lands while US exchanges are shut, and the date is so public it feels like a sure thing.
What Is Driving It

Reuters reported that Truth Social is set for release on Monday in Apple's App Store [[n0932]], and Axios carried the same debut [[n1766]], after Reuters said the app had opened to hundreds of testers [[n1742]]. The fine print is less exciting: Nunes said the app will be fully operational by the end of March, according to The Guardian [[n1765]], so Monday is a front door rather than a finished building. The tape is hostile: the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.14% to 14,009.54 index points on February 18, the VIX closed at 27.75 index points and Robinhood Markets dropped 11.34% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). DWAC's 2.83% five-session gain against that backdrop says it trades on its own calendar.
The Social Signal

Attention is abundant, and its shape is the tell. Newsweek's first look said Truth Social looks almost identical to Twitter [[n1723]], Vanity Fair told readers to get ready for Retruths [[n1744]], and Snopes found it worth fact-checking whether the app will cost users $4.99 a week [[n1755]], the kind of claim that only gets checked once it is travelling. None of that counts buyers, but a stock whose catalyst is a consumer app lives on mainstream curiosity: everyone who learns the date is a potential download and, for some, a DWAC order. Leverage cuts both ways: Wolf Street reports margin debt plunged as high-fliers got crushed, yet leverage is still gigantic [[n1310]], fuel for an unwind if the gap disappoints.
Historical Analog

The sharpest analog is days old. Virgin Galactic surged 30% after the company announced $450,000 tickets to space, Forbes reported [[n0523]]; by Friday SPAC King Chamath Palihapitiya had abruptly resigned as chair amid a stock crash [[n0903]], and SPCE closed at 8.40 USD, down 6.77% on the day and 0.47% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The pop round-tripped inside a week, and the mechanics map onto DWAC: a dated consumer event, a SPAC wrapper, a famous sponsor and a crowd buying the date rather than the economics. The longer memory is 2021, when Avis briefly achieved meme-stock status and soared 456%, as Business Insider recounted [[n1713]]. In spikes like these, the event tends to be the exit for early holders rather than the entry for latecomers.
Smart Money View

Professional opinion splits over the business, not the ticker. The chief executives of Parler and Gettr welcomed Trump's platform, Bloomberg reported [[n1730]], a sign the audience is real but contested; The New York Times says Truth Social is poised to join a crowded field [[n1767]], and Time asks whether it can compete with mainstream social media [[n0403]]. Above it all, Charlie Munger says retail trading apps are creating a speculative mess (Yahoo Finance) [[n1721]], while Bloomberg carries Themis Trading's Joe Saluzzi on what it calls the retail investors' rebellion [[n1737]]. Professionals will judge monetisation over quarters; the crowd will likely judge the launch by its first days in the App Store.
When the Narrative Breaks

The first test is Tuesday's open. DWAC has not traded since its 84.32 USD close on February 18, so the launch, its reception and a weekend in which the BBC reported Biden is convinced Putin has decided to invade [[n1424]] arrive in one gap. The bulls' line is the 73.12 USD close of January 21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18): a break below it would erase the whole 15.32% run into the launch and stamp this a sell-the-news event. The second test is Nunes's own end-of-March timetable [[n1765]]: a phased rollout that leaves would-be users waiting is the anticlimax that turns a lottery ticket into a bag. And a blank-check shell priced on the Trump Media deal story, not on Truth Social revenue, can gap on headlines that have nothing to do with downloads.

retail.title: Bitcoin / BTC-USD — digital gold flunks the weekend war test
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Crypto is the only market retail could trade all weekend, and it voted early: Bitcoin closed at 38,431.38 USD, down 4.21% on the day and 13.78% over five sessions, while Ether fell 17.33% to 2,628.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-20). Dip-buyers call it the bargain the Super Bowl blitz advertised, a message Bloomberg summed up as stop worrying and just buy crypto [[n0360]]. The awkward part: The Seattle Times says the crypto ad millions did not drive downloads [[n0086]], and Ethereum founder Buterin says crypto welcomes another winter, per Bloomberg [[n1001]].
Where It Breaks

Digital gold is losing its own head-to-head: gold futures rose 3.13% over five sessions to 1,899.80 USD/oz while Bitcoin's 20-session change slipped to -0.13%, handing back February's bounce (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18; Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-20). CNBC frames its bitcoin outlook around geopolitical tensions heating up and rates rising [[n2045]]. Marathon Digital, at 23.89 USD, and Coinbase, at 189.16 USD, last traded before the weekend slide (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), leaving Tuesday a gap to absorb; if they reprice lower while Bitcoin stays below its January 31 close of 38,483.12 USD, the dip becomes the trend.

retail.title: ARK Innovation ETF / ARKK — Cathie Wood keeps the dip-buying faith
parts: Why Retail Is Here

ARKK is the congregation's fund, and its preacher is unwavering: Cathie Wood says her innovation stocks are way undervalued and recent fund losses temporary, CNBC reports [[n1741]], and warns investors are making one of the greatest misallocations of capital in history, per Business Insider [[n1757]]. The sermon lands on a fund that fell 4.96% on February 18 to 64.80 USD and 9.87% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Believers read every leg lower as a bigger rebound ahead, and pandemic winners like Roblox, down 25.58% over five sessions on sales The Boston Globe says the COVID decline hurt [[n1109]], as inventory on sale.
Where It Breaks

Bloomberg notes ARKK is a year from its peak and still struggling [[n1720]], and the reason sits in the bond market: the 2-year Treasury yield is 1.47%, up 46 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18), and long-duration growth absorbs that repricing first. Roblox's worst post-earnings drop, which Bloomberg said wrecks the stock-pop narrative [[n0117]], shows what happens when a temporary story meets a soft quarter. The faith breaks if ARKK keeps failing below its January 21 level of 71.52 USD while short yields climb.

retail.title: Gold Miners ETF / GDX — the old haven still earns its keep
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Gold is the war hedge retail's parents would recognise, and it works: gold futures closed at 1,899.80 USD/oz, up 3.13% over five sessions, while the GDX miners ETF rose 6.38% to 34.50 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The BBC reports Biden is convinced Putin has decided to invade [[n1424]], Reuters says Putin will oversee nuclear drills [[n1422]], and Axios reports Russia extended drills in Belarus, fuelling invasion fears [[n1435]]. Miners are the geared expression, hence GDX outrunning the metal, and GLD made Yahoo Finance's list of top trades for Tuesday [[n0834]].
Where It Breaks

The haven trade is a bet on escalation, so diplomacy is its enemy: The Guardian reports Macron has paved the way for a potential Putin-Biden summit [[n1430]], and real de-escalation would drain the fear premium, hitting miners hardest. Rates are the second risk, the subject of a Visual Capitalist explainer on how interest-rate hikes affect gold's price [[n1776]], and Barrick's chief executive suggests miners are overpaying for assets amid higher gold prices (Financial Post) [[n0705]]. A GDX slide back toward its January 21 close of 31.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) would say the war premium has gone.
